title: Mayrovitz 2020 · forearm local heater 42 °C · skin surface
citation: Mayrovitz HN et al. (2020). Effects of local forearm skin heating on skin properties. Clin Physiol Funct Imaging. https://doi.org/10.1111/cpf.12653
measurementNote: Published IR skin temperature immediately after heater removal (mean ± SD across n=30). Not a continuous under-heater T(t) series.
extractedFromPaper: 20 mm aluminium local heater on dominant anterior forearm
Heater held at 42 °C for 12 min after ramp from 35 °C
Immediate uncovered post-heat IR skin temperature 39.5 ± 1.9 °C
Skin blood flow increased 8.8-fold from the 35 °C baseline
Authors judge under-heater skin during the hold was between 40 and 42 °C
unknowns: Continuous under-heater skin T(t) was not published — only preheat and immediate post-removal IR points from the text
Exact interface film and strap pressure not quantified
35 °C pre-hold and 90–120 s ramp are collapsed into an ideal 42 °C hold for the locked protocol
